questions.question: With close reference to the two films you have studied, explore how either performance or mise-en-scène create meaning. (sample paper)
traps: “With close reference to the two films” = both films, in depth. Comparison earns no extra marks.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
Every paragraph needs a named scene AND a named technique (your teacher’s target 1).

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Choose ONE element and analyse how it creates meaning in both films.
indicative: Mise-en-scène: Vidal’s uniform and the farmhouse in the bottle murder; the Pale Man’s banquet and shoes; the labyrinth motif
City of God: the favela growing cramped; the apartment; guns and gold
Performance: López’s chilling precision; Baquero’s stillness; City of God’s non-professional cast
Meaning linked to context: fascism; state neglect
Aesthetic dimension: gothic fairytale vs kinetic realism

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis (mise-en-scène): in both films mise-en-scène turns setting into argument: the fantasy mirrors fascism, the favela shows the cycle of neglect.

P1 The bottle murder: Vidal’s uniform and the cold farmhouse. P2 The Pale Man’s feast and shoes. P3 The Story of the Apartment. P4 The favela closing in over the decades.

Conclusion: mise-en-scène is where each film’s politics becomes visible.

questions.question: With close reference to the two films you have studied, explore how either editing or sound create meaning. (sample paper)
traps: “With close reference to the two films” = both films, in depth. Comparison earns no extra marks.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
Every paragraph needs a named scene AND a named technique (your teacher’s target 1).

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Choose ONE element and analyse how it creates meaning in both films.
indicative: Editing: City of God’s freeze-frames, 360° spin, apartment dissolves
Pan’s Labyrinth’s wipes between worlds; cross-cutting at the climax
Sound: the lullaby motif; sweetened violence; Rocket’s voiceover; ironic funk and samba
Meaning: cycles of violence; fantasy as resistance
Spectator response to rhythm and sound

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis (editing): editing creates each film’s structure of meaning: cycles in City of God, mirrored worlds in Pan’s Labyrinth.

P1 Chicken chase. P2 Apartment. P3 Wipes. P4 Final cross-cutting.

Conclusion.

questions.question: Apply one filmmaker’s theory of documentary film you have studied to your chosen documentary. How far does this increase your understanding of the film? (sample paper)
traps: “How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.
Name the filmmaker’s theory precisely and explain its central ideas before applying it.
Every paragraph needs a named scene AND a named technique (your teacher’s target 1).

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (10) and AO2 (10) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Clarify one theory (Longinotto, Broomfield, Moore or Watkins), apply it to Amy, judge how far it helps.
indicative: Longinotto: invisible filmmaker, fiction-like identification, no conclusions
Amy: invisible Kapadia, audio-only interviews, identification with Amy
Differences: Amy uses captions, music and an implied conclusion about blame
Techniques conveying the real: home video, on-screen lyrics
Band 5: documentaries can only give an ideological representation of their subject

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: Longinotto’s theory increases understanding to a large extent, because Amy shares her invisibility and identification, but its implied blame shows where Kapadia departs.

P1 Invisibility: no talking heads; audio over footage. P2 Identification: the birthday video and lyrics. P3 Departures: score, edit-driven blame, paparazzi sequences.

Conclusion.

questions.question: “Portable digital cameras, digital sound recording and non-linear digital editing have had a very significant impact on documentary film.” How far has digital technology had an impact on your chosen documentary? (sample paper)
traps: “How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.
Name the filmmaker’s theory precisely and explain its central ideas before applying it.
Every paragraph needs a named scene AND a named technique (your teacher’s target 1).

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (10) and AO2 (10) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Both sides of the digital debate, applied to Amy.
indicative: Non-linear editing of vast archive; reframing low-res images
Counter: compilation films and tragic narratives pre-date digital

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: very significant: Amy could not exist without digital recording, though its storytelling is traditional.

P1 Footage. P2 Editing. P3 Counter-argument.

Conclusion.
